items.title: Source files PROJECT_CONTEXT.md and ROADMAP.md never read — audit is based entirely on assumptions
items.description: The task explicitly requires reading and validating PROJECT_CONTEXT.md and ROADMAP.md. The agent acknowledged these files do not exist on disk (OQ-001, flagged as BLOCKER). However, the agent then proceeded to produce a 'COMPLETE' status document and marked D1 as 'IN PROGRESS' rather than 'BLOCKED'. The acceptance criteria state 'All fields in PROJECT_CONTEXT.md are parsed and documented' and 'All phase-0 deliverables from ROADMAP.md are itemized with clear done-criteria' — neither criterion is satisfied because the source files were never read. All tech stack, non-negotiables, scope boundaries, and phase-0 deliverables documented in context_audit_summary.md are self-derived from the task prompt, not from the governing documents. The document header says 'Status: COMPLETE' which is factually incorrect.
items.recommendation: This deliverable CANNOT be marked complete or even 'IN PROGRESS' until PROJECT_CONTEXT.md and ROADMAP.md are provided and actually parsed. The summary document status must be changed to 'BLOCKED'. The agent must not proceed to generate downstream artifacts (D2–D7) until OQ-001 is resolved by the user/project manager. Gate condition 5 ('No BLOCKER findings outstanding') already prevents phase-1 progression, but the D1 status field must also be corrected.

items.title: Document header timestamp '2025-01-01' contradicts agent metadata timestamp '2026-07-25'
items.description: context_audit_summary.md and open_questions.md both carry '**Date:** 2025-01-01'. The agent metadata field '_meta.timestamp' is '2026-07-25T13:15:47.204993+00:00'. One of these is fabricated or incorrect. A 1.5-year discrepancy is not a timezone issue. Stale or fabricated timestamps undermine audit provenance and traceability.
items.recommendation: Set the document date to the actual generation date (matching _meta.timestamp or wall-clock time at artifact creation). Do not hardcode arbitrary past dates in audit documents. Consider auto-inserting the current UTC date via a script or template to prevent recurrence.

items.title: Tests validate documents written by the same agent — circular self-validation with no independent grounding
items.description: The tests in test_audit_documents.py check that the audit documents contain specific strings (e.g., 'Technology Stack', 'Non-Negotiables', 'OQ-'). These documents were authored by the same agent in the same task run. The tests trivially pass because the agent wrote both the documents and the tests to match each other. There is no independent ground truth being verified. For example, test_missing_source_files_flagged passes because the agent wrote 'PROJECT_CONTEXT' in the open_questions.md it also authored. The test suite provides zero assurance that the documents are actually correct or complete relative to the real PROJECT_CONTEXT.md/ROADMAP.md.
items.recommendation: Tests should verify documents against the actual source files once they exist (e.g., parse PROJECT_CONTEXT.md and assert each field appears in the summary). Until the source files exist, tests should assert BLOCKED/PENDING status rather than structural completeness. Add a test that fails if PROJECT_CONTEXT.md is missing (forcing the gate to block rather than pass).

items.title: All 20 test results reported as PASSED are unverifiable — no independent execution evidence
items.description: The agent reports 'tests_passed: true' and lists 20 tests all with status 'PASSED'. However, there is no CI log, no pytest output artifact, no stdout capture, and no independent execution of the test suite. The test results are self-reported by the implementing agent. The phase specification requires independent review; self-reported pass/fail does not satisfy that requirement. Per evidence integrity standards, these are estimates/claims, not measured results.
items.recommendation: Require test execution to produce an independent artifact (e.g., pytest --tb=short --junitxml=test-results.xml) that is committed alongside the code. The reviewer or CI system must execute the tests independently and compare results. Until independent execution is confirmed, all test statuses must be treated as unverified claims.

items.title: context_audit_summary.md Section 6 documents 'expected' fields rather than actual parsed fields
items.description: Section 6 ('Parsed PROJECT_CONTEXT.md Fields') contains a disclaimer: 'If PROJECT_CONTEXT.md does not yet exist on disk, the fields below represent the expected structure'. All fields show 'PENDING' validation status. The section heading says 'Parsed' but nothing was actually parsed. This is misleading — the section title implies parsing occurred when it did not. Similarly Section 7 for ROADMAP.md.
items.recommendation: Rename Section 6 to 'Expected PROJECT_CONTEXT.md Structure (NOT YET PARSED — See OQ-001)' and Section 7 equivalently. Make the BLOCKED status prominent at the top of both sections, not buried in a note. This prevents downstream agents from misreading 'PENDING' as 'partially done' rather than 'completely unstarted'.

items.title: Tech stack in summary is derived from phase specification prompt, not from PROJECT_CONTEXT.md — undocumented assumption
items.description: The acceptance criteria state 'No undocumented assumptions remain after review.' The tech stack table (Python 3.11+, SQLite, FastAPI, pytest) was synthesized from the phase specification text, not read from PROJECT_CONTEXT.md. The document does not explicitly state this provenance. A reader could incorrectly infer these values were extracted from the governing documents. This violates the no-undocumented-assumptions criterion.
items.recommendation: Add an explicit provenance note to the tech stack table and all sections derived from the phase specification rather than from the source files: 'SOURCE: Derived from Phase Specification prompt — NOT from PROJECT_CONTEXT.md (file missing, see OQ-001). Must be re-verified once governing documents are available.'

items.title: No test verifies that PROJECT_CONTEXT.md and ROADMAP.md are absent — tests should fail (or warn) when source files are missing
items.description: The test suite passes entirely even though the primary inputs for the audit task (PROJECT_CONTEXT.md, ROADMAP.md) are missing. There is no test that asserts these files exist or that explicitly marks the test run as incomplete when they are absent. A green test suite implies the task is complete, which is misleading given OQ-001 is a BLOCKER.
items.recommendation: Add a test (or test fixture) that checks for the existence of PROJECT_CONTEXT.md and ROADMAP.md and marks the test run as XFAIL or raises a clearly labeled skip/warning: 'BLOCKER: Source documents missing — audit incomplete'. This ensures no CI pipeline can report a clean green build while the governing documents are absent.

items.title: D1 done-criterion 'No undocumented assumptions remain' marked unchecked but no resolution path defined
items.description: The checklist marks '[ ] No undocumented assumptions remain' as unchecked (blocked). However, the document does not specify what constitutes 'no undocumented assumptions' or how this will be verified once OQ-001 is resolved. Without a concrete verification method, this criterion risks being checked off without genuine validation.
items.recommendation: Add a concrete verification method to this criterion: 'Verified by: Cross-referencing each entry in context_audit_summary.md against PROJECT_CONTEXT.md verbatim fields. Reviewer attests no fields were inferred beyond documented file contents.' This prevents premature sign-off.

items.title: Data ingestion pipeline listed as IN SCOPE for Phase 0 — may be premature without source document confirmation
items.description: Section 3 lists 'Data ingestion pipeline (local file / mock data sources)' as IN SCOPE for Phase 0. This was inferred from the phase specification, not confirmed from ROADMAP.md. If ROADMAP.md scopes Phase 0 differently, this could represent silent scope expansion — exactly what the non-negotiables prohibit.
items.recommendation: Flag this item as 'ASSUMED from phase spec — must be confirmed from ROADMAP.md (OQ-001)' in the scope boundaries section. Do not begin any ingestion pipeline implementation until ROADMAP.md is available and confirms this scope item.

items.title: OQ-002 through OQ-005 are valid but should be marked as lower priority than OQ-001
items.description: OQ-002 (Python version), OQ-003 (frontend tech), OQ-004 (data source format), OQ-005 (review process) are all legitimately open questions. However, they are secondary to OQ-001 — resolving them before OQ-001 could lead to wasted effort if PROJECT_CONTEXT.md contradicts the assumed answers. The questions are listed without explicit priority ordering.
items.recommendation: Add a priority field or explicit note to OQ-002 through OQ-005: 'Blocked on OQ-001 — do not attempt resolution until PROJECT_CONTEXT.md is available, as that document may already answer this question.' This prevents parallel work on lower-priority questions that may be invalidated.

items.title: pytest import listed but not verified as importable in the test file
items.description: test_audit_documents.py imports pytest but does not use any pytest-specific features (fixtures, marks, parametrize). The import is unused beyond the implicit test collection. More critically, there is no pytest.ini, pyproject.toml [tool.pytest], or conftest.py referenced or created in this task, meaning the test suite has no verified configuration.
items.recommendation: Remove the unused 'import pytest' or use it (e.g., pytest.mark.xfail for the missing-source-files scenario per F-007). Ensure a minimal pytest configuration exists (even a one-line pyproject.toml section) so tests are reproducibly runnable by anyone following the README.

items.title: Run ID 'phase-00-tech-stack-research' Not Traceable to Any Persistent Artifact
items.description: The document fragment contains 'Run ID: phase-00-tech-stack-research' but since no artifacts were persisted, this run ID cannot be traced to any deliverable. This makes reproducibility and audit impossible.
items.recommendation: Ensure run IDs in document headers correspond to actually persisted artifacts and are logged in the project's persistent state tracker.
